title: Fenrir recipe
description: One server kind as data: how to get it, run it, configure it, tell when it is ready, count its players, stop it, update it and back it up. Fenrir 3, recipes.md. Data only: a recipe never carries code; built-in recipes may name a built-in hook.

id.description: Stable id. For the six 2.x servers it is their 2.x kind (valheim, palworld, sevendays, terraria, fivem, skyrimtogether).

version.description: The recipe's own version, not the game's.

size.description: Disk use in words, shown before install (2.x hosting.SIZES).

icon.description: A file beside the recipe in the library, 64 KB at most.

license.description: The recipe's own licence (the data), required in the library.

client.description: The game friends play, by store id: what Fenrir Connect looks for on a friend's PC (2.x recipe 'client').

antiCheat.description: The owner's rule (PLAN-V3 section 7, answers 1 and 20): a game whose anti-cheat cannot be switched off on its server gets no recipe at all. One whose anti-cheat can be switched off is allowed when Fenrir keeps it off: the recipe names the anti-cheat and every switch Fenrir keeps off, and the validator checks that the recipe really keeps each one off.

status.description: none: the server has no anti-cheat. off: it has one, and Fenrir keeps it off with the switches in keepOff. Anything else is refused by the validator.

what.description: The anti-cheat by name (Easy Anti-Cheat, VAC, Terraria's cheat protection).

keepOff.description: Every switch that would turn it on, each one kept off by Fenrir (status off).

platforms.description: Where the server itself runs (not the game's client).

firstRun.description: Steps run once after install, before the first start (initdb, an EULA file).

platformOverrides.description: What differs on one platform, merged over the recipe there (Valheim's Linux program and library path).

rcon.description: How Fenrir reaches the server's Source RCON, for an rcon probe, player source, stop step or chat: the port, and the secret setting that holds the password. A Minecraft world needs none: its driver knows its RCON.

secrets.description: Sealed values Fenrir makes for each server once, at its first start, and keeps in the store as server.<id>.<name>: a password only Fenrir uses (Palworld's admin password for its own web API, V Rising's RCON). Never written in a recipe, never shown on a page; writers name one as {secret.NAME}, a REST call's auth and RCON as secret.NAME.

hooks.description: Built-in recipes only: the Python class in core/recipes/hooks that adds what data cannot say. The validator refuses hooks in library, local and imported recipes.

research.description: Where the facts come from: the 2.9 rule that each recipe keeps its research notes beside it.

status.description: How sure the recipe's facts are: live-checked once a real server has run it; until then the research's own confidence, lowered where the recipe leans on facts no source confirmed (the notes say which).

regex.description: A Python regular expression applied to one log line (4 KB at most). The validator refuses backreferences, lookbehinds and nested quantifiers (recipes.md section 5).

template.description: Text with placeholders: {setting.KEY}, {setting.KEY+N}, {port.ID}, {port.ID+N}, {install} (the server's program folder; for get.fromGame the game's own folder, read only), {data} (the server's own folder, DATA/games/servers/<id>), {saves}, {log}, {game}, {profile}, {address} and {code} (join texts only), {secret.NAME} (a sealed value of this server's own, server.<id>.NAME in the store; env, files and the connection string only), {name} and {text} (chat and player commands only), {minutes} (stop.warn only). A secret setting's {setting.KEY} goes on the command line only with inArgs, and never into a text that friends or the phone see. Anything else in braces stays as written, as 2.x fill() does.

antiCheatSwitch.description: One switch Fenrir keeps off: an argument never passed, arguments always passed, a key one of the recipe's writers sets at every start, or an environment variable always set.

noArg.description: Never on the command line, whatever the settings say (Terraria's and V Rising's -secure).

args.description: Always on the command line, never behind a condition (a Source server's -insecure).

file.description: A writer's file, written exactly as that writer names it.

key.description: The key as that writer names it (7 Days to Die's EACEnabled, V Rising's /Secure, The Forest's enableVAC).

value.description: What the writer sets it to at every start (false, off): written as it is, never from a setting.

override.description: run, stop and saves take the override's keys over their own; get, firstRun and backup are replaced whole (a program's name differs by platform: initdb.exe and initdb).

secretRef.description: A secret the server keeps sealed in the store: one of the recipe's secret settings (setting.KEY), or a value Fenrir made for it (secret.NAME, from secrets). Opened by the driver when it is used; never written in a recipe, never sent by a page.

auth.description: HTTP Basic authentication for a call to the server's own web API on this PC (Palworld's REST API): the user as the game names it, the password from the server's sealed store.

strip.description: Leading folders to drop when unpacking.

rename.description: For unpack none: the file's name in {install}.

anonymous.description: Fenrir never signs in to Steam (PLAN-V3 P1.3). A server that needs an owning account is said plainly and has no recipe.

platform.description: SteamCMD's +@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType, when the server's build is not the host's own platform's.

workshop.description: The game's app id for Workshop items, where anonymous download works.

resolver.description: Built-in recipes only: a named Python resolver finds the current URL (FiveM's download page). Its result is still checked against an allow-list of hosts.

hosts.description: With a resolver: the only hosts its URLs may name.

file.description: Relative to the game's own folder; never .. (Terraria's TerrariaServer.exe).

keep.description: Top folders of the server's own copy left alone on refresh (Skyrim Together's config).

digest.description: Pinned in the library; a local recipe may follow the tag.

none.description: Your own server: nothing to install, Fenrir runs the program the host picked.

if.description: Present when the setting is on (a switch) or not empty (text): 2.x 'flags', and the dropped empty -password (servers.py 338-344).

unless.description: true: present when the setting is off or empty instead.

program.description: Relative to {install} (or {data}), never ..; an absolute path only for kind own, and only one the host picked in Fenrir's own dialog (2.x custom.py 263).

realPrograms.description: What a launcher starts in turn, for the firewall rule (2.x Palworld realExes).

portEnv.description: An environment variable that carries the first port (2.x your own server sets PORT).

console.description: How a console line reaches it: its input pipe, key presses into its own console (2.9 your own server), or not at all.

shell.description: cmd only for kind own with a .bat or .cmd (2.9 custom.py 431-436, with command_problem).

output.description: Where its own lines are: its output, or the file its arguments make it write (2.x 7 Days to Die -logfile, servers.py 419-422).

friends.description: Friends need it from outside: router, firewall, tunnel, direct connections.

http.description: It speaks HTTP: a site's port, which the front door and quick tunnels can serve.

path.description: Where the world or data is: inside {data}, {install}, or (when the game cannot be told) {profile}.

how.description: How the path is chosen: by an argument, a variable or a config key Fenrir sets, fixed by the game, under the account's profile, or picked by the host (own).

whileRunning.description: How a backup reads it while the server runs.

portable.description: The world's files work on every platform the recipe lists, so a move between Windows and Linux carries them as they are (server.md section 3.7). Unknown means a move stays on one platform.

notIn.description: Must not be part of these settings' values (Valheim: the password may not be in the name).

as.description: A switch as text where it is written (Valheim -public 1 or 0).

span.description: A port setting that takes this many ports from its value up (the clash check, QoL 6).

inArgs.description: A secret that goes on the command line because the game takes it nowhere else: visible to other programs on this PC, said in the trust prompt.

restart.description: A change needs a restart to take effect.

phone.description: What Fenrir Link may do with it (secrets are write-only there anyway).

file.description: Inside {install} or {data}; resolved and checked at every write.

from.description: A template file the server ships, copied first (2.x 7 Days to Die serverconfig.xml).

set.description: xml-property: property name. ini: Section/key, the key after the last slash, so an Unreal section works (/Script/Icarus.DedicatedServerSettings/MaxPlayers). ini-tuple: Section/Key/Field, one field inside a key whose value is an Unreal struct in brackets (Palworld's OptionSettings=(...)). properties and keyvalue: key. json: a JSON pointer (/a/b). Only these keys change; the rest of the file stays as the server or the host left it.

lines.description: format lines: the whole file, one template per line.

hook.description: format hook, built-in recipes only (FiveM's server.cfg with its ensure lines).

when.description: Written at every start (2.x write_config) or when the host saves the setting.

once.description: Write the file only while it is not there: a default the server itself would make on its first start and then stop for (Sons of the Forest's ownerswhitelist.txt), which the host edits afterwards.

keepIfSet.description: ini-tuple: keys left as the file has them when it already gives them a value (a password the host set there themselves).

port.description: A TCP port that accepts a connection, or a UDP port whose query answers.

alive.description: Running this many seconds counts as ready: for a game Fenrir cannot ask. Said in the trust prompt and on its page.

on.description: With query: which port to ask.

restartAfter.description: Unhealthy this many times in a row: restarted (0: only said).

names.description: a2s: also ask A2S_PLAYER for names while someone is on (2.5).

count.description: log: a line that carries the count in group 1 (Valheim crossplay's 'is active with N player').

join.description: log: a join line, the name in group 'name'.

url.description: rest: a URL on this PC (127.0.0.1) only.

path.description: rest: a JSON pointer to the list or the count.

auth.description: rest: HTTP Basic authentication, its password from the server's sealed store.

sources.description: Tried in order; the first that answers counts. None answering means 'cannot tell', which a stop from the phone treats as people on (2.x servers.py 435-456).

kick.description: A console or RCON command, {name} filled in.

do.description: close: the program asked to close, as taskkill without /F does on Windows (what Core Keeper's own launcher does) and SIGTERM on Linux.

line.description: command: one plain console line (2.9 PLAIN_STOP).

body.description: rest: the request's body, {setting.KEY} and {port.ID} filled in (and {minutes} in a warning).

auth.description: rest only: HTTP Basic authentication, its password from the server's sealed store.

grace.description: Seconds from the first step until the whole tree is ended (2.x stopWait).

warn.description: What tells players before an update or a planned restart, {minutes} filled in (P1.6 'warn players'): a console line, or a step: a console command, an RCON command or a REST call (the server's own broadcast).

stopWords.description: Console words that would end it behind Fenrir's back: refused, its Stop or Restart offered instead (2.9 custom.py STOP_WORDS).

previous.description: The branch where the game keeps its version before the newest: a rollback with no copy of the server's files installs it.

version.description: A JSON pointer to the version in the feed.

community.description: The Thunderstore community, or CurseForge's game slug.

travel.description: The host's game mods go on the server too (2.x hosting.server_mods), and friends get the client side.

code.description: The log line that carries this run's code in group 1.

steamArgs.description: Fenrir Connect starts the game pointed at the server (2.x connectArgs).

passwordSay.description: Add 'Then type the server's password.' when one is set (2.x WITH_PASSWORD).

log.description: A chat line, with groups 'name' and 'text'.

escape.description: json: the text inside a JSON string (Minecraft tellraw). quotes: inside double quotes. strict: letters, digits, spaces and . , ! ? ' - only.

compose.description: A compose file beside the recipe, instead of one image.

versions.description: Where the list of versions comes from.

java.description: The lowest Java per Minecraft version (2.x loaders.java_major_for).

game.description: The game itself must be installed (fromGame).

harness.description: How the fake server behaves for this recipe (recipes.md section 3.10).

live.description: One live smoke run on this PC where its disk allows, the download deleted after (PLAN-V3 section 7, answer 8; fenrir/build/live_recipe.py writes it).

build.description: The build id (or version) of the server the live run checked.

loopback.description: How the live run tells the server to listen on 127.0.0.1 only, so Windows Firewall has nothing to ask: arguments added to its command line, settings given, or keys its writers also set. A recipe without one says plainly that a firewall prompt may appear.
